items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1970-02-14
items.q: See, George Washington played with us all the while.

ctx.x: Um, did I have to play with, um, with Buddy Bowden?

Yeah, well, I played a while there, but we had George Washington. George was the main man. See, George Washington played with us all the while. It was just when George couldn't play while he did how well, you know.
He was a pretty good comment man, wasn't he? Was that, O.O? Oh, yeah.

items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1966-03-09
items.q: Well that's really because I couldn't read at that time myself. But George he could read a little bit, and I think Edmund could read

ctx.x: down, you know if he ever wrote any, or composed any, made them up or anything.

No. No. No. Sometime you take like, he get a number, and if he learned a number, he's going to come tell us, well we've got a new number. We just try it before people come in. We're going to play right there. All right after the banjo, get on in there and him and this boy, and that. Well them three they're going to slow, you know what I mean? Well a little while after that I come on in there and I'm hitting, you know what I mean? After I be hitting like that, well that tramo was going to come in there. So Edmund…

Yeah Buddy could spell. But he was fine boy though. I was going to ask you again about your very early life, which you didn't tell so much about when you were going over that material. You were born 1900 you say? That's right. Can you tell us anything about your parents? Did they play any instrument?
